meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Now tell me what you based it on.
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
"Like, being stuck" is a fair definition from a seventeen-year-old cornered by his teacher without warning. Show me the note you wrote that day.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their thesis between an outline and a final draft, that's the point of drafting. Put the outline and the essay side by side in front of me, and the note from November 2.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's your own procedure for a first concern, and nothing on his record is what I came for, so put it in writing tonight, not Friday after he's already sat it. I haven't agreed to a rewrite. You still owe me the outline, the essay, and your November 2 note.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record, and you committed to putting that in writing by Friday at 3 PM. I still require that commitment in writing before Owen sits anything, along with copies of his October 15 outline, his essay, and your note from November 2. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: The fallback position; your offer of the procedure 4.4 terms met her demand that nothing go on his record, but she had not agreed to the rewrite and still wants it in writing tonight and to see the outline, the essay and your November 2 note, which is close to the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record (procedure 4.4), and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You committed to the 4.4 terms, with the rewrite mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, which answered the one thing she will never trade.
What cost ground: You described your evidence and then made the offer without ever showing her the documents, so she had nothing she could check and no reason to accept a rewrite.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence was an outline from mid-October and a conversation on November 2, so it never came near a late night, and that window proves nothing about the essay, it is only why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to see your November 2 note, put the note and the October 15 outline beside the essay in front of her before you made any offer.
